policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'with the poor', which renders the ketiv עניים (from עָנִי, poor/afflicted), not the qere עֲנָוִים (from עָנָו, meek/humble). The qere sense is relegated to the margin: the note 'Or, meek' is classed alternative_rendering and does not itself decide, but the choice of 'poor' in the text over 'meek' matches the ketiv's lemma and is the distinguishing wording.

ASV reads 'And in his lips there is as a scorching fire' — plural 'lips', matching the ketiv שפתיו (dual/plural with suffix) rather than the singular qere שְׂפָת֗וֹ 'his lip'. Grammatical number is visible in the English and ASV renders it here; the only note on the verse ('Hebrew diggeth', hebrew_gloss) concerns the verb and is silent on this unit.
